newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end lower on Wall St, volume shrinks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end lower on Wall St, volume shrinks.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended down for a second day in a row, again mirroring Wall Street, on lower turnover than usual, brokers said.

The Bovespa index of the 49 most active shares closed off 0.98 percent at 9,172 points. Market volume was just 483.1 million reais ($455.7 million), below the market's recent daily average of $600 million.

Analysts said local shares followed U.S. stocks, which fell on investor caution ahead of Wednesday's release of key economic data that may indicate if the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee will raise rates or not at its next meeting.
They also said the market suffered from press reports about the alleged involvement of Sao Paulo mayor Celso Pitta in a multi-million state and municipal debt scandal.

Senator Roberto Requiao, who is heading a congressional probe into the bond scam, told reporters he had evidence that Banco Vetor, allegedly involved in the fraud, paid a car rental bill of $2,500 for Pitta's wife.
Analysts feared the implications of the probe if Pitta's involvement is proved to be true.
The bolsa was marginally hit at lunch time by rumors, denied by Brazilian authorities, that Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola had handed in his resignation, traders said.
